The Center for Peace and Global Citizenship (CPGC) cooperates with students and faculty in all majors to advance justice, inclusion, and sustainability by linking experiential learning with the needs and desires of off-campus partners. This linking occurs through student fellowships that support systematic, ongoing professional development coupled with internships during the summer and throughout the academic year. Beyond these fellowships, the CPGC also supports community-engaged courses, research, and scholarship. This work - at the heart of positive peace-building and critical global citizenship - occurs in Ardmore, in the Philadelphia Region, and all around the world.

For service and advocacy opportunities in Ardmore, as well as student volunteer clubs and community-based work study, visit the Marilou Allen Office of Service and Community Collaboration.

Fellowships

A CPGC Fellowship is a funded opportunity for Haverford students to gain experience advancing peace, justice, inclusion, or sustainability - while developing professional skills.

M. Gessen Visits Haverford to Talk Autocrats and Hopeful Politics

The Pulitzer Prize winner visited campus for a wide-ranging conversation on autocracy, institutions, and what it takes to build something better.

Summer Centered: Adam Chen '29 Traces His Story Through a Cup of Tea

The prospective chemistry major spent five weeks in China researching a centuries-old tea ritual. He returned stateside with a clearer picture of his Chinese identity.

Summer Centered: Luka Idiart Tous '29 Confronts the Housing Crisis in Madrid
The prospective political science major spent his summer supporting tenants facing eviction, displacement, and skyrocketing rents.
Summer Centered: Erik Fagerstrom '27 Untangles a Citizenship Limbo

Between a Gurkha citizenship brief, a tourism report, and a stint working for a member of parliament, Erik Fagerstrom '27 spent his summer at the center of Nepali policymaking.

Sumita Lacey '26, named the 2026 Publicly-engaged Scholar!

The CPGC is excited to announce Sumita Lacey as the 2026 Publicly-engaged Scholar, honoring her work in her senior thesis to explore collective power in Kensington. This year’s cohort of award nominees each engaged in impactful, community-involved research, exemplifying Haverford’s mission to merge academic excellence with meaningful societal contribution.

2026 Publicly-engaged Scholar Nominees

We invite you to join the Center for Peace and Global Citizenship in celebrating this year’s nine nominees for the 2026 Publicly-engaged Scholar Award, on Monday, April 27, at 4:30 p.m. in Lutnick 200. 

2026 CPGC Fellows Announced!
Congratulations to the 52 students awarded 2026 Fellowships with the Center for Peace and Global Citizenship! This summer, Fellows will undertake internships across the globe with organizations advancing peace, justice, inclusion, and sustainability. These Fellowships build on more than 1,200 internships supported by CPGC since 2001.
Hafiz Tunis Jr. Receives Haverford's 2026 MLK Award

Upper Darby Township's youngest and first Black council president was nominated by student Izzy Muraca '26 for his community-centered approach to public service.

CPGC Celebrates This Year's Inspiring Student Fellows!

On October 23, 2025 Haverford College students, faculty, staff, and broader community members filled Lutnick Library for the annual CPGC Poster Fair and Ignite Presentations, an inspiring evening of reflection, shared learning, and celebration of students’ summer experiences advancing peace, justice, inclusion, and sustainability locally and around the world.
